deciding_assertions: pydantic.md mixin section: MyModel.__init__ reveals (self: MyModel, *, mixin_field: LaxBool, model_field: LaxBool, **extra: Any) -> None; MyModel(model_field=True, mixin_field=False) gives no unknown-argument error
reason: The issue asks that annotated fields of a non-BaseModel mixin count as model fields. The narrowest reasonable fix collects fields from every class in the pydantic model's MRO; base-first order and the LaxBool type follow from existing field collection and match the runtime output in the issue. It passes both assertions.

deciding_assertions: constructor.md: class Bar with @classmethod __new__ -> Self; Bar() keeps too-many-positional-arguments (expected 0, got 1) and reveal_type(Bar()) is Bar
reason: The issue says the diagnostic is correct and the result should be Foo, not <class 'Foo'>. A fix that solves Self to the instance type for a classmethod-bound __new__ keeps the existing diagnostic and gives Bar; this is the issue's own case with another class name.

deciding_assertions: aliased_conditions.md: is_none = x is None; if y := is_none: reveal_type(x) is None, else int (needs the alias-predicate walk in the semantic index builder to see through a named expression)
reason: The issue lists isinstance, TypeGuard, TypeIs and `is` comparisons directly as the walrus value. A reasonable fix evaluates the walrus value as a normal predicate in narrow.rs and drops constraints on the rebound target; it passes the isinstance, is, ==, type guard and overwritten-target tests, but not the aliased-condition test, which needs a separate change to how alias predicates are registered. Aliased conditions through a walrus are not stated in the issue.

deciding_assertions: unpack.md 'Invalid unpack contexts still infer the operand': def invalid_context(value: Unpack[Missing]) must also report unresolved-reference; def invalid_stringified_context(value: "Unpack[Missing]") must report only invalid-type-form (no unresolved-reference); also new reveal list[tuple[Unknown, ...] | None] for list[Union[Unpack[int], None]]
reason: The issue only reports a panic for list[Union[Unpack[], None]]. A fix that removes the double inference and keeps the early returns passes the crash test but does not report unresolved-reference for Unpack[Missing]; a fix that always infers the operand reports unresolved-reference in the string annotation too, which the test forbids. The silence rule for invalid string annotations is a new behaviour the issue does not give.

deciding_assertions: useless-return snapshot: `return None  # c` becomes exactly `    # c` (spaces before the comment removed); `print(sys.version); return  # c` becomes `print(sys.version); # c`; `return (  # c\n None\n)` keeps deletion but is marked unsafe
reason: The issue asks only that the trailing comment be preserved. A reasonable fix that deletes only the statement range leaves the original spaces before the comment, or that marks the fix unsafe or skips it when a comment is present, fails the exact snapshot. The unsafe marking for a comment inside a parenthesized return value is a case the issue does not state.

deciding_assertions: pydantic.md: Person(name="Alice", something_else=7) and the extra="ignore" model must report error: [pydantic-discarded-extra-argument] by default; extra="allow" gives no diagnostic
reason: The issue asks for a configuration option with no fixed name and calls its own name a placeholder. The test needs a new lint named pydantic-discarded-extra-argument that is on by default; a fix with another option or lint name, or with the check off by default, fails.

deciding_assertions: invalid_syntax.md: case [] | [last_value]: last_value must report possibly-unresolved-reference (and the middle-alternative, nested, guard and partial-overlap variants); the issue's malformed case only needs no panic plus the syntax errors
reason: The issue is one panic for `case b|c b:`. A reasonable fix of that crash (model the merge of capturing alternatives, or handle the visible implicit unbound at the lookup) need not change the old path where a capture-free first alternative skips the flow merge, so `case [] | [last_value]` still gives a definitely bound name and fails. These flow-modeling cases are not stated in the issue.

deciding_assertions: external/pydantic.md mixin section: reveal_type(MyModel.__init__) is (self: MyModel, *, mixin_field: LaxBool, model_field: LaxBool, **extra: Any) -> None; MyModel(model_field=True, mixin_field=False) gives no unknown-argument
reason: The issue asks that annotated fields of a non-BaseModel mixin become init parameters of the Pydantic model. The narrowest reasonable fix lets the Pydantic field collection include such bases in the existing MRO walk; it passes the call check, and the field order (base fields first) and LaxBool come from the existing collection and display.

deciding_assertions: call/constructor.md class Bar with @classmethod __new__(cls) -> Self: reveal_type(Bar()) is Bar, plus the too-many-positional-arguments diagnostic for bound method Bar.__new__
reason: The issue asks that Self in a classmethod-decorated __new__ resolve to the instance type Foo, not <class 'Foo'>, while the existing diagnostic stays. Any fix that binds Self to the instance type passes reveal Bar; the diagnostic text is the existing one, as the Foo(1) test above it shows.

deciding_assertions: isinstance.md, type_guards.md, is.md, eq.md: `if result := <predicate>(value)` narrows value in if/else; overwritten-target cases (`value := (value is None)`, `value := guard_list(value)`, `value := (value.tag == 'a')`) keep only truthiness narrowing of the new value; aliased_conditions.md: `if y := is_none:` narrows x to None / int
reason: The issue says most kinds of narrowing fail on the walrus value and lists isinstance, TypeGuard, TypeIs and `is`; a general fix evaluates the value as a normal narrowing condition, which also covers `==` and an aliased condition name. The overwritten-target tests keep existing behaviour, and a correct fix must not apply old-value constraints to the rebound name. The aliased-name case needs a second code path (the alias walk), so a reader could call it an extra case; I count it as a direct variant of 'any narrowing condition as walrus value'.

deciding_assertions: generics/legacy/unpack.md 'Invalid unpack contexts still infer the operand': `def invalid_context(value: Unpack[Missing])` must also report [unresolved-reference] Name `Missing`, while `"Unpack[Missing]"` in a string annotation must report no unresolved-reference
reason: The issue only reports a panic for `list[Union[Unpack[], None]]`. The narrowest reasonable fix stops the double inference of the Unpack operand in the Union path and keeps the early return for invalid contexts, so `Unpack[Missing]` in a parameter annotation reports no unresolved-reference and fails the test; a fix that always infers the operand fails the string-annotation case unless it adds the same speculative silencing. Both behaviours are new design choices that the issue does not ask for.

deciding_assertions: useless-return snapshot: exact fix output `# comment` kept on its own indented line, `print(sys.version); # comment` for a same-line return after a semicolon, `return; # c` becomes `# c`, and the fix for `return (  # comment\n None\n)` marked unsafe
reason: The issue only says the comment should be kept. Reasonable fixes differ: mark the fix unsafe or skip it when a comment is present, or keep the comment in another layout (for example `print(sys.version)  # comment` without the semicolon). The snapshot fixes one exact layout and also needs unsafe applicability for comments inside a parenthesized return, which the issue does not mention.

deciding_assertions: external/pydantic.md: Person(name='Alice', something_else=7) and the extra='ignore' model now expect `# error: [pydantic-discarded-extra-argument]` by default; tests changed to extra='allow' to stay silent
reason: The issue asks for an opt-in configuration option with no fixed name. The tests need a new lint rule named pydantic-discarded-extra-argument that is on by default; no fix from the issue can guess that name, and an opt-in option would leave the default-config calls silent and fail.

deciding_assertions: invalid_syntax.md: the issue's `case first | second first:` gives only the three invalid-syntax errors; or-patterns that bind different names give [possibly-unresolved-reference] for captures missing from some alternative (first/second, [x] | [], [] | [x], middle, nested, guard), no error for shared captures or for a name bound before the match
reason: The panic comes from merging or-pattern alternatives so that a capture and the implicit unbound state are both definitely visible; a fix of that cause must model the alternatives as exclusive branches, and then ty's existing semantics give possibly-unresolved-reference for partial captures, as for if/else. The extra test cases are the same mismatched-names situation with other patterns. A fix that silently treats all captures as bound would fail, so a reader could decide otherwise.

deciding_assertions: pydantic.md JsonValueModel: list, dict, str, int, float, bool, None and nested JSON values give no error; object(), ... and SomethingElse() give [invalid-argument-type]; nested {"inner": SomethingElse()} gives no error (TODO line)
reason: The issue asks to remove the top-level Any from the lax JsonValue type and gives the expected shape list[Divergent] | dict[str | bytes, Divergent] | str | bool | int | float | None. A fix that produces that shape (or only removes the top-level Any) accepts all valid values, rejects object(), ... and an arbitrary class instance, and keeps Divergent in recursive positions, so the nested case gives no error. No revealed type or message is checked.

deciding_assertions: dataclasses.md: `if not is_dataclass(event)` with event: Event reveals Never; new check_class with event_type: type[Event] reveals Never
reason: The issue asks that the negative is_dataclass branch for a concrete dataclass narrows to Never. The class-object case is the same function through its other overload, which the issue's own revealed type (~type[DataclassInstance]) and the earlier top-materialization behaviour cover. A fix at the root (typeshed return type or the gradual protocol member) fixes both; a fix that handles only instances would be a partial fix of a direct variant.

deciding_assertions: in.md: inline list/set membership narrows positive and negative branches (Literal["a","b"] / Literal["c"]); literal_locals with a = "a"; mixed_literals with int, bytes and None; union_valued_slots gives no narrowing; str & ~Literal["a"] & ~Literal["b"] in the negative branch for x: str; assert_never exhaustiveness
reason: The issue names tuples as the reference: `value in [a, b]` and `value in {a, b}` should narrow like `value in (a, b)`, including the else branch. A fix that treats an inline list or set like a tuple of its element types gives every expected result, since all assertions mirror tuple narrowing. A fix that only accepts string literal AST nodes would fail literal_locals and mixed_literals, but those are direct variants (other literal values, the issue's own `[a, b]` form).

deciding_assertions: functions.md: takes_in_type_of_list(list[int]) -> int, (Sub) -> int, (GenericSub[str]) -> str; create(Specialized) -> tuple[int, str]; get_value_for(StringOption) -> str; infer(sink, 1) -> Literal[1] and infer_bounded(sink, "ok") -> Literal["ok"] in a contravariant position; infer(Final[int]) -> int for a final generic class
reason: The issue asks that T in type[Option[T]] is inferred from a class object whose bases specialize Option. A general fix infers type arguments for any class object passed to type[C[T]] (class literal, generic alias, final class, several type variables), which covers the direct variants. The contravariant tests pass before the fix and pass for a fix that respects the existing polarity handling; only a fix that ignores variance would break them, which is not a correct general fix. A reader could see the final-class and contravariant cases as extra cases.

deciding_assertions: pydantic.md: Settings(), Settings(host=...), Settings(port=...), Settings(host=..., port=...) give no error; Settings(host=None) gives [invalid-argument-type]; extra keyword still gives [unknown-argument]
reason: The issue asks that BaseSettings subclasses do not require field arguments, as with the mypy plugin. The narrowest fix gives every field of a BaseSettings subclass a default in __init__ and keeps the field types; it passes all calls without or with some arguments, still rejects None for a str field, and keeps the existing unknown-argument check.

deciding_assertions: attributes.md: class-object writes through metaclass __setattr__ accepted for int and rejected for str with the existing "with custom `__setattr__` method" message (also via type[Foo] and when the class has its own __setattr__); setter type gives context to lambda and TypedDict values; name overloads; Never-returning setter gives [invalid-assignment] "Cannot assign to unresolved attribute"; protocols.md: protocol assignments keep their current errors (TODO lines), Foo.x = 1 writes accepted
reason: The issue names instance-level __setattr__ as the reference and asks that metaclass __setattr__ is honored for class-attribute writes. A fix that runs the existing instance __setattr__ path against the meta-type gives the same messages, contextual inference, overload choice and Never handling. The protocol tests only need protocol satisfaction to stay as it is, which the issue does not ask to change; a fix that also changed protocol checks would go beyond the issue.

deciding_assertions: pydantic.md JsonValueModel: list, dict, str, int, float, bool, None and nested values give no error; object(), ..., SomethingElse() give [invalid-argument-type]; nested SomethingElse inside a dict gives no error (TODO line)
reason: The issue asks to remove the top-level Any from the lax JsonValue type and keeps Divergent (gradual) in recursive positions. The narrowest reasonable fix (give float a lax alias, or build the list | dict | str | bool | int | float | None shape) accepts every listed value and rejects the top-level objects. The nested case stays accepted because the issue itself keeps recursive positions gradual. The tests do not check the revealed display, tuple or UserDict.

deciding_assertions: dataclasses.md: `not is_dataclass(event)` for event: Event reveals Never; new case `not is_dataclass(event_type)` for type[Event] reveals Never
reason: The instance case is the issue's own example. The class-object case is the other argument kind of the same public function, and the same root cause (the gradual protocol member) decides it, so a fix of the subtyping or of the is_dataclass return type covers both. A fix that special-cases only instances is narrower than a general fix of the stated cause. Medium because the issue offers more than one fix route, and I cannot see the rest of the mdtest file that a typeshed member change could touch.

deciding_assertions: in.md: list and set literals narrow like tuples for in / not in, positive and negative; literal locals [a, b]; mixed literals with bytes and None; union-valued slots give no negative narrowing; assert_never exhaustiveness; x: str gives str in the positive branch and str & ~Literal["a"] & ~Literal["b"] in the negative branch
reason: The issue names tuple membership narrowing as the reference and asks for the same narrowing for inline list and set literals. The natural fix treats the list or set literal like a fixed tuple of its element types in membership narrowing. Every assertion then matches the existing tuple behaviour. Medium because a fix that accepts only syntactic literal elements (not locals with literal types) would fail literal_locals; the issue's own text uses `xxx in [a, b]` with names, so I count that as a direct case.

deciding_assertions: functions.md: takes_in_type_of_list(list[int]) -> int, (Sub) -> int, (GenericSub[str]) -> str; create(Specialized) -> tuple[int, str]; Options().get_value_for(StringOption) -> str; contravariant Sink[type[Covariant[T]]] gives Literal[1] and Literal["ok"]; infer(Final[int]) -> int for a @final generic class
reason: The issue asks to infer T when a class object is matched against type[Generic[T]]. A general fix infers type arguments from the class object's specialized bases and handles class literals, specialized aliases, more than one type variable and methods, which are direct variants. The contravariant test keeps existing behaviour and passes when the fix respects variance. Medium because the @final case uses a different internal form of type[Final[T]], and a fix that misses it would fail, although for the user it is the same operation.

deciding_assertions: pydantic.md: Settings(), Settings(host=...), Settings(port=...), Settings(host=..., port=...) give no error; Settings(host=None) gives [invalid-argument-type]; the existing unknown-argument error stays
reason: The issue asks that BaseSettings fields do not need to be passed to the constructor, as with the mypy plugin. The narrowest reasonable fix makes every field of a BaseSettings subclass an optional keyword parameter that keeps its declared type. It passes all calls, and host=None still fails because the field type is str. The test does not check a signature display.

deciding_assertions: attributes.md: Foo.whatever = 42 accepted, = "invalid" gives [unresolved-attribute] "with custom `__setattr__` method"; metaclass method wins over the class's own __setattr__; type[Foo] path; lambda and TypedDict values get the setter's value type as context; name-specific overloads; Never-returning metaclass setter gives [invalid-assignment] "Cannot assign to unresolved attribute `new`"; Frozen.existing = 2 stays accepted; Regular.whatever still errors. protocols.md: ClassWithDynamicX.x = 1 accepted; protocol assignment results unchanged (TODO errors kept)
reason: The issue names the instance-level __setattr__ path as the reference. A fix that resolves undeclared class-attribute writes through the metaclass __setattr__ with the same evaluator logic (existing BadSetAttr and TerminalSetAttr messages, call with the literal name, contextual value inference) passes every assertion. Fixes that also change protocol satisfaction or block writes to declared attributes change behaviour that the issue does not ask to change. Medium because the lambda and TypedDict assertions need type context from the setter; I assume the instance path already gives that context, but I cannot confirm it from the packet.

deciding_assertions: typed_dict.md: `def _(item: Item | str)` with `isinstance(item, dict)` then `reveal_type(dict(item))` is `dict[str, object]`; new HasClear test: `reveal_type(clear_result(value))` is `None` after `isinstance(value, HasClear)`
reason: The first assertion is the issue's own case (wide TypedDict union plus str, narrowed by isinstance dict, passed to dict()), and the expected type is the one the direct TypedDict-union case already gives. The narrowest reasonable fix makes the narrowed intersections reuse the common-constraint path while keeping the intersection semantics, which passes both; the HasClear test only guards existing behaviour against a lossy fix that drops the narrowing constraints, which point (3) rules out.

deciding_assertions: type_guards.md 'Overloaded definitions': one_invalid gets exactly one invalid-type-guard-definition error at the invalid overload's return annotation with the existing message; two_invalid gets one error on each invalid overload with its own types
reason: The issue says the diagnostic is correct but must appear once; the bug is that each overload check reports every overload's problem at its own location. The narrowest reasonable fix checks each overload once at its own return annotation, which passes both the issue's case and the two-invalid-overloads variant; the message text is the existing one.

deciding_assertions: redundant-numeric-union.md: no PYI041 diagnostic at all on `@dispatch.register def _(value: int | float)`; PYI041 still raised for `@dispatch.register(int | float)`; still raised (with fix) for a second parameter `other: int | float` of a registered function; no diagnostic for a singledispatchmethod registration and in a .pyi stub
reason: The issue reports that the --fix is incorrect; a reasonable fix keeps the diagnostic and removes the fix (or marks it unsafe) for registered functions, and that fix fails the test that expects no diagnostic. The tests also pin cases the issue does not name (explicit register(...) still flagged, only the first parameter exempted, singledispatchmethod skipping self), so a fix that exempts every parameter of any `.register`-decorated function fails them.

deciding_assertions: exhaustiveness_checking.md: match on FallbackColor (custom _missing_) from a function is exhaustive, assert_never passes; match_custom_missing_enum has no invalid-return-type; eq.md: singleton enum with _missing_ gives `left == right` Literal[True] and `left` Never under `!=`; identity and cross-enum comparisons with _missing_ enums reveal the declared-member types
reason: The issue states that a custom _missing_ cannot add members, so the enum's declared members are a closed set. The narrowest general fix stops treating custom _missing_ as making the enum open, and all assertions are direct consequences of a closed member set, matching existing behaviour for enums without _missing_; the tests replaced the old object.__new__ examples, so a fix that still treats object.__new__ as open also passes.

deciding_assertions: callables_as_descriptors.md: `class Thunk: __value_thunk__: Callable[[], int]` with `self.__value_thunk__ = other.__value_thunk__` gives no error and `reveal_type(Thunk().__value_thunk__)` is `() -> int` (new rule: the dunder heuristic does not apply to zero-parameter callables); dunder.md: `value.__call__` is `(str, /) -> int` and `value("value")` is int for `__call__: Callable[P, int]`
reason: The dunder.md assertion is the issue's case and a fix that stops the function-like dunder heuristic for ParamSpec callables passes it. The Thunk test adds a separate rule for zero-argument dunder callables that the issue does not mention (the real fix adds a `has_parameters` check for it), so the narrowest reasonable ParamSpec fix leaves that behaviour unchanged and fails the test.

deciding_assertions: protocols.md: `takes_read_class` reveals `ReadClass[int | float]` (read-only __class__ keeps the float promotion); `takes_writable_value` reveals `WritableValue[int | float]` (a writable type[T] member not named __class__ keeps the promotion); plus takes_just_float(1.0) accepted, takes_just_float(1) and (True) rejected, `Timestamp() * 1.0` is Timestamp
reason: The issue asks only that Just[float] accept a float, as in mypy and pyright. Several designs do that (for example, no int/float promotion inside type[T] after substitution, or no promotion for any protocol type argument used as type[T]); the tests pin one narrow special case (only protocols that declare a writable __class__ of type[T]), and broader reasonable fixes fail the ReadClass and WritableValue reveal assertions.

deciding_assertions: typed_dict.md: after isinstance(item, dict) on Item | str, reveal_type(dict(item)) is dict[str, object]; HasClear runtime protocol narrowing of ClearA | ClearB keeps clear_result(value) revealed as None
reason: The first assertion is the issue's own case, and its expected type equals the existing result for the unnarrowed TypedDict union. The narrowest reasonable fix makes the narrowed intersections reuse the TypedDict-union optimization and passes it. The HasClear test is existing fallback behaviour; only a fix that drops the intersection's protocol constraints breaks it, and that fix changes behaviour the issue does not ask to change.

deciding_assertions: type_guards.md 'Overloaded definitions': one_invalid reports the existing message once, on the invalid overload only; two_invalid reports one diagnostic on each invalid overload (bool/Never and str/int)
reason: The issue says the diagnostic is correct but must appear once, on the overload that is wrong. A fix that checks each overload against its own signature once gives exactly these diagnostics with the existing message. Only a hack that keeps the first diagnostic for each function fails two_invalid, and that is not a correct general fix.

deciding_assertions: redundant-numeric-union.md: no PYI041 on the dispatch parameter of @dispatch.register functions (py, pyi, singledispatchmethod with self); PYI041 still on the singledispatch base function, on other parameters (snapshot with existing message and fix), and on @dispatch.register(int | float) explicit registrations
reason: The narrowest reasonable fix skips PYI041 for the dispatch annotation of a singledispatch registration, for example with the existing is_singledispatch_implementation helper. It passes the issue's case and the singledispatchmethod variant. The other sections check behaviour that already exists and that the issue does not ask to change. Medium: a fix that keeps the diagnostic and only removes the autofix would fail, but the diagnostic itself is wrong advice in this case.

deciding_assertions: exhaustiveness_checking.md: match on MissingValueEnum / FallbackColor with custom _missing_ is exhaustive (assert_never passes, no invalid-return-type); eq.md: single-member _missing_ enum left == right is Literal[True], left != right narrows to Never, and cross-enum comparisons of _missing_ enums narrow like closed enums
reason: The issue asks that a custom _missing_ not make the enum open, because _missing_ must return a valid member. The natural fix removes the _missing_ condition from the enum's closed-member check. The match and equality narrowing both follow from that check and match the existing behaviour of enums without _missing_. Medium: the eq.md changes are consequences that the issue does not state outright.

deciding_assertions: callables_as_descriptors.md Thunk: __value_thunk__: Callable[[], int] must not be made function-like (reveal () -> int, and the assignment self.__value_thunk__ = other.__value_thunk__ gives no error)
reason: The issue is about a ParamSpec Callable[P, ...] dunder class variable. The dunder.md test checks that case and is fair. The real fix also adds a separate rule that zero-parameter dunder callables skip the descriptor heuristic (has_parameters), and the Thunk test checks it. A fix that keeps ParamSpec dunder callables regular solves the issue but does not change zero-argument callables, so it likely fails the Thunk test.

deciding_assertions: protocols.md: takes_just_float(1.0) ok, takes_just_float(1)/(True) error; Timestamp() * 1.0 revealed Timestamp; takes_just_union(1)/(1.0) error; ReadClass[float] and WritableValue[float] still reveal int | float
reason: The issue states that Just[float] must accept a float and exclude int and bool, as mypy and pyright do. The narrowest reasonable fix stops the float promotion for Just-like protocols (a __class__ getter and setter of type[T]) and passes those assertions. The explicit-union, ReadClass and WritableValue checks are existing behaviour that the issue does not ask to change. Medium: the scope of the special case is a design choice, and a broader or type-level fix would break these checks.

deciding_assertions: mdtest refurb/subclass-builtin.md, section 'Stub files': no FURB189 diagnostics on dict, list, str and subscripted dict[str, str], list[str] subclasses in a .pyi file
reason: The issue asks that FURB189 not apply to stubs. The narrowest reasonable fix returns early from the rule when the source type is a stub, which emits no diagnostic for any class in the .pyi block and passes the test.

deciding_assertions: call/builtins.md: isinstance(x, (A, B)) with x: A | B reveals Literal[True] and accepts_a_or_b / accepts_stored_tuple give no invalid-return-type; isinstance(x, (A, (B, bytes))) and isinstance(x, (A | B,)) and isinstance(items, (List,)) must reveal bool; (RuntimeProtocol,) reveals bool; (RejectingBase,) and (type,) reveal Literal[True]
reason: The issue's case is x: Foo with isinstance(x, (Foo, Bar)). The narrowest reasonable fix ORs the single-class truthiness of each tuple element: it solves the issue but gives bool for a union input x: A | B, so it fails the reveal_tuple_result and accepts_a_or_b assertions. A fuller fix that also handles nested tuples or union elements, which isinstance accepts at runtime, fails the assertions that these stay bool, a limit the issue never states.

deciding_assertions: diagnostics/error_context.md snapshot: returning D as Mapping[str, int] still gives invalid-return-type, with info 'TypedDict `D` is not assignable to `Mapping[str, int]`' and two new help lines about closed=True and subclass unsoundness
reason: The issue asks ty to accept a uniform TypedDict as Mapping[str, int]. A fix that does this removes the error and fails the snapshot, which keeps the error. Even a fix that keeps the error fails, because the snapshot needs exact new info and help texts that the issue does not give.

deciding_assertions: directives/cast.md snapshot 'Fixes preserve comments in parenthesized arguments': cast(val=( # Leading comment. x + y # Trailing comment. ), typ=int) must be fixed to the parenthesized text with both comments kept; also pass-to-pass redundant_cast_without_closing_parenthesis (incomplete call must not panic)
reason: The narrowest reasonable fix wraps the value text in parentheses when it spans lines. It gives exactly the expected output for the issue's conditional case and both multiline arithmetic cases, but for the keyword val=(...) case the value x + y is on one line, so it emits 'return x + y' and drops the comments, which fails the snapshot. The issue does not mention comments or keyword arguments.

deciding_assertions: mdtest ruff/method-receiver-default.md selects RUF077 and expects [method-receiver-default] errors, snapshot message 'Receiver parameter should not have a default value' and fix title 'Remove default value from receiver parameter' with an unsafe fix; settings::tests::preview_default_rules lists 'method-receiver-default (RUF077)'; no error for any decorated method other than a sole @classmethod
reason: The issue gives no rule code, name, message or tool. Any reasonable fix (a ty diagnostic, or a ruff rule with another code or name) fails the test that needs RUF077 and method-receiver-default by name and the exact snapshot texts. The decorator exclusions (for example @override with self=None gives no error) are a design choice that the issue does not state.

deciding_assertions: named_tuple.md: '# error: [invalid-named-tuple] "Type qualifier `ClassVar` is not allowed on NamedTuple field `a`"' and the same for Final; two separate errors for c: ClassVar[Final[int]]; snapshots with exact text 'Type qualifier `ClassVar` is not allowed in a NamedTuple field' and no further sub-diagnostics
reason: Using the existing invalid-named-tuple rule follows from the repo, but the issue gives no message. A reasonable fix that reports this under invalid-named-tuple with other wording (for example 'NamedTuple field `a` cannot be declared ClassVar') fails the message assertions and both snapshots. Reporting one error, not two, for ClassVar[Final[int]] is also reasonable and fails.

deciding_assertions: refurb/subclass-builtin.md: no FURB189 diagnostic in a .pyi block for class D(dict), L(list), S(str), dict[str, str] and list[str] subclasses
reason: The issue asks that FURB189 not apply to stub files. The narrowest reasonable fix (return early when the source type is a stub) passes the new mdtest, which only asserts no diagnostics in a stub. The subscripted bases are direct variants of the issue's dict/list/str case.

deciding_assertions: call/builtins.md: reveal_type(isinstance(x, (A, (B, bytes)))) revealed: bool; reveal_type(isinstance(x, (A | B,))) revealed: bool; plus Literal[True] for flat tuples and stored tuples
reason: The issue asks that a tuple isinstance check covering the value be treated as always true for reachability. A reasonable, more general fix that also follows nested tuples or union elements (both valid isinstance forms at runtime), or one that derives truthiness from narrowing to Never, infers Literal[True] for these cases and fails the asserted bool limits. The narrow flat-tuple fix passes, but the limits are a design choice the issue does not give.

deciding_assertions: diagnostics/error_context.md snapshot: return d still gives invalid-return-type, with info 'TypedDict `D` is not assignable to `Mapping[str, int]`' and two exact help lines about closed=True and subclass unsoundness
reason: The issue asks that an open TypedDict with uniform int values be accepted as Mapping[str, int]. The test keeps the error and only adds new help text. The narrowest reasonable fix (accept the assignment) removes the diagnostic and fails the snapshot; any fix that keeps the error also needs the exact new wording.

deciding_assertions: directives/cast.md snapshots: multiline ternary keeps its parentheses; unparenthesized multiline 'x +\n y' and 'x\n + y' get new parentheses; keyword val=( # comment ... ) before typ= keeps its parentheses and comments
reason: The issue shows a parenthesized multiline ternary whose parentheses the fix drops. A reasonable general fix (wrap the value in parentheses when it spans lines) passes the first three snapshots but drops the comments in the last case, which the issue never mentions; a fix that only keeps the value's own parentheses fails the two unparenthesized arithmetic cases. The snapshots fix one exact output text for each.

deciding_assertions: ruff/method-receiver-default.md: rule method-receiver-default (RUF077), message 'Receiver parameter should not have a default value', fix title, unsafe fix output; no error for any decorated method (@override, custom decorator, property setter); settings::tests::preview_default_rules lists method-receiver-default (RUF077)
reason: The issue asks for a new error for defaults on self or cls but gives no rule name, code, message or fix. Any reasonable new rule needs the exact name RUF077/method-receiver-default and exact texts to pass; a fix that also flags decorated methods fails the no-error block.

deciding_assertions: named_tuple.md: error: [invalid-named-tuple] "Type qualifier `ClassVar` is not allowed on NamedTuple field `a`" (and Final variants); two separate errors for ClassVar[Final[int]]; snapshots with 'not allowed in a NamedTuple field' and the field range
reason: The issue asks to flag ClassVar and Final on NamedTuple fields; the rule invalid-named-tuple exists, but the issue gives no message. A reasonable fix with any other wording fails the quoted-message assertions and snapshots, and a fix that reports one error for ClassVar[Final[int]] fails the double-error assertion.

deciding_assertions: aliased_conditions.md: with is_none = (x is None), `if y := is_none:` reveals x as None / int and y as Literal[True] / Literal[False]; eq.md and is.md: `value := (value is None)` and `value := (value.tag == "a")` reveal Literal[True]/Literal[False] (constraints on the rebound target dropped); isinstance.md, type_guards.md, eq.md, is.md: `result := <check>(value)` narrows value
reason: The narrowest reasonable fix makes the walrus value go through the normal predicate evaluation in narrow.rs. It passes the isinstance, TypeIs, TypeGuard, `is` and `==` cases, and the rebound-target cases follow from keeping existing behaviour. It fails aliased_conditions.md: narrowing through an aliased condition inside a walrus needs a separate change in the semantic index builder, and the issue does not mention aliased conditions.

deciding_assertions: invalid_syntax.md: `case [] | [last_value]:` and `case [] | [middle_value] | []:` expect possibly-unresolved-reference; also partial-overlap, nested-alternative, guard and prior-binding cases; the issue case (`case first | second first:`) expects only the three syntax errors
reason: The issue asks only that ty stop panicking on one malformed match case. A fix that removes the panic passes the malformed-recovery section. But the tests also need a new model of invalid or-patterns that bind different names. One example: when the first alternative captures nothing, the old shortcut leaves later captures definitely bound, so no possibly-unresolved-reference error is reported. A crash fix does not need to change that, so it fails these assertions.

deciding_assertions: redundant-numeric-union.md: `@dispatch.register def _(value: int | float)` (also the singledispatchmethod and .pyi variants) must give no PYI041 diagnostic at all; later parameters and explicit `register(int | float)` must still be flagged
reason: The issue reports that the --fix edit is wrong for a singledispatch-registered function. It does not say that the diagnostic is wrong. One reasonable fix keeps the diagnostic and removes the fix, or marks it unsafe. That fix fails the mdtest, because the test expects no diagnostic. A fix that skips the first annotated dispatch parameter (the existing is_singledispatch_implementation helper covers singledispatchmethod) passes all sections.

deciding_assertions: protocols.md: takes_just_float(1.0) ok, takes_just_float(1) and (True) error; takes_just_int(True), (1.0) error; takes_just_union(1) and (1.0) error; reveal_type(Timestamp() * 1.0) is Timestamp; ReadClass[float] and WritableValue[float] still reveal [int | float] and takes_read_class(1) is ok
reason: The issue names mypy and pyright as the reference: Just[float] accepts a float and rejects int and bool. Any correct fix must stop the float-to-int|float promotion in Just's type argument, which also gives the union and int results by protocol semantics. The getter-only ReadClass and the non-__class__ WritableValue assertions only check existing behaviour, so a narrow fix keyed on Just's read/write __class__ of type[T] passes them. A fix that also changes the getter-only protocols would fail them, so the result depends on how strictly 'keep existing behaviour' is read.
